newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay share index drops 2.9 pct, SBI leads fall.
newsitem.headline: Bombay share index drops 2.9 pct, SBI leads fall.

text.p: Share prices fell sharply at Bombay bourses on Friday as nervous investors began a sell-off behind falling SBI stocks, brokers said.
"Depressed SBI prices acted like a catalyst to trigger the selling spree," said one trader. "The market had been waiting for something to happen -- and the news was negative."
SBI fell 10.50 rupees to 228.50 at the BSE as players saw little prospects for the stock in the near-term with foreign fund holdings reaching the 20 percent cap set by the government.
The share was down 8.5 rupees at 231.75 on the National Stock Exchange.
The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index fell 93.56 points, or 2.93 percent, to a provisional 3,102.21 close after sliding to 3,095.14.
The 50-stock NSE index dropped 18.95 points, or 2.05 percent, to a provisional 906.05.
"It's a blood bath," said one dealer at a foreign broking firm. "There's panic everywhere."
Traders said foreign and domestic funds were sellers. ITC, MTNL, ICICI, Bajaj Auto, TELCO, SBI, Century Textiles, Century Enka were some of the shares sold by the funds.
Telephone stock MTNL shed 13.75 rupees to 199.25 at the BSE.
Analysts said sentiment was also undermined by lingering worries of political instability after a Congress party warning to the ruling minority coalition government.

The new Congress party chief said on Thursday that its crucial support to the government depended on reciprocal backing for the Congress in India's most populous state of Uttar Pradesh where local elections are currently underway.
TELCO fell 40.25 rupees to 393, Bajaj Auto 33 to 950.50, Indian Hotel 27.75 to 636.75, Hind Lever 27 to 785.75, Hindalco 28.75 and Glaxo 10.25 to 195.
